metadata.content: Ryan Garcia set to face US rival Teofimo Lopez next after emphatic victory over Conor Benn | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ryan Garcia set to face US rival Teofimo Lopez next after emphatic victory over Conor Benn After his spectacular stoppage of Conor Benn, Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez next; Benn is yet to confirm his next career move although he continues to be linked with a trilogy fight against Chris Eubank Jr; Garcia and fellow American Lopez are both welterweight world champions Thursday 15 October 2026 17:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Garcia retained his WBC world title after flooring Conor Benn heavily before forcing a stoppage victory in the second round. Fight footage courtesy of DAZN Ryan Garcia is set to face Teofimo Lopez in his next fight after his emphatic victory over Conor Benn last month. Garcia defended his WBC welterweight title with a second-round stoppage of British contender Benn in Las Vegas and is now holding talks for a fight against Lopez, Sky Sports News understands. Fellow American Lopez also holds a world title in the same division after he sealed a majority decision win over Rolando Romero to claim the WBA belt in August. messages.text: Infantino sorry for World Cup plan and set to ditch award previously given to Trump

metadata.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday - and the Peace Prize he awarded to US President Donald Trump looks set to be ditched.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign Gianni Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council for his World Cup sell-off plan; FIFA president was speaking in Zurich on Thursday morning; the FA is among European leaders who still want him to resign, while UEFA has called on Infantino to release documents related to the scheme Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Thursday 15 October 2026 20:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gianni Infantino says he apologised for 'mistakes in relation to the communication and consultation process' for World Cup sell-off plan FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday - and the Peace Prize he awarded to US President Donald Trump looks set to be ditched. Infantino's expression of regret for not telling the council about his plans earlier was not good enough for European football leaders, including FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who still want him to resign. UEFA wants Infantino to release all documents relating to the plan as they believe the 20 per cent stake in all future FIFA tournaments was being sold for a knockdown price.
